evals.name: typescript-order-service-refactor
evals.prompt: Refactor this order service to follow strict quality patterns. The code is at skills/code-quality/evals/files/eval1_order_service.ts.
evals.expected_output: Refactored TypeScript with all `any` types replaced by proper types, immutable data (no mutation of order or items), pure calculateTotal function, early returns instead of nested conditionals in createOrder, Result types instead of thrown errors for business logic, createOrder parameters collapsed into an options object, @ts-ignore removed, and comments replaced by self-documenting function names.
expectations: Removes all `any` type annotations — calculateTotal parameter typed as Order, processRefund return typed as a discriminated union or Result type, not `any`
Replaces `as any` cast in applyCoupon with a properly typed structure (extends the item type or uses a new type)
Removes @ts-ignore directive and handles the error type properly (unknown + type narrowing)
Makes applyCoupon return a new order object instead of mutating the existing one (order.discount mutation eliminated)
processRefund does not mutate order.status — returns a new object or uses a Result pattern
Replaces nested if/else pyramid in createOrder (total > 10000 block) with early returns or guard clauses
Collapses createOrder's 7 positional parameters into a single options object or interface
Uses declarative transformation (map/reduce) instead of imperative for-loop in calculateTotal
Uses a Result or discriminated union return type for error cases instead of throwing errors for business logic (validation failures, user not found)
anti_expectations: Does not use `any`, `as Type`, or `@ts-ignore` in the refactored code
Does not add comments explaining what code does — code should be self-documenting through naming
Does not leave mutable operations on function arguments (no direct property assignment on passed-in objects)
Does not silence the type checker with escape hatches

evals.name: python-analytics-quality-pass
evals.prompt: Apply code quality patterns to this Python analytics module. File is at skills/code-quality/evals/files/eval2_analytics.py.
evals.expected_output: Refactored Python with all `Any` types replaced by specific types, frozen dataclass for Event, pure compute_top_events using Counter or comprehension instead of imperative loop, merge_event_properties returning a new dict instead of mutating base, no `# type: ignore` directives, dependency injection for I/O in AnalyticsTracker, and datetime.now(tz=UTC) instead of naive datetime.
expectations: Removes all `Any` type annotations — Event.properties typed with specific types or `object`, function return types use concrete types not `Any`
Removes all `# type: ignore` directives (in filter_events_by_date and parse_event_from_json) and fixes the underlying type issues
Makes Event dataclass frozen (frozen=True) to enforce immutability
Rewrites merge_event_properties to return a new dict (`{**base, **override}` or `base | override`) instead of mutating the base argument
Rewrites compute_top_events using Counter or a declarative approach instead of the imperative counting loop with the off-by-one bug
Rewrites filter_events_by_date using a list comprehension instead of an imperative loop with append
Injects I/O dependencies into AnalyticsTracker (file writer, API key) via constructor parameters instead of reading os.environ and writing directly to filesystem
Replaces class-level mutable `_events: List[Event] = []` with instance-level initialization to avoid shared state across instances
anti_expectations: Does not use `Any`, `cast()`, or `# type: ignore` in the refactored code
Does not add docstrings or comments explaining what functions do — uses self-documenting names instead
Does not leave the singleton pattern with hardcoded I/O (os.environ access, direct file writes) embedded in business logic
Does not mutate function arguments (no in-place dict updates on parameters)

evals.name: typescript-cache-module-cleanup
evals.prompt: Clean up this cache module following strict code quality principles. Source at skills/code-quality/evals/files/eval3_cache.ts.
evals.expected_output: Refactored cache module with all `any` replaced by generic type parameters, CacheEntry made readonly, module-level mutable Map replaced with injected dependency, pure getStats function, warmCache using Promise.all instead of sequential await in loop, proper error handling with Result types instead of silent catch, and as CacheEntry assertion removed.
expectations: Removes all `any` types — uses generic type parameter `<T>` for cache value types (getOrSet<T>, warmCache<T>, setWithRetry<T>)
Makes CacheEntry properties readonly to enforce immutability
Removes `as CacheEntry` type assertion in setWithRetry and constructs the object with proper typing
Replaces module-level mutable `const cache: Map` with an injected dependency (passed as parameter or via constructor of a class)
Injects the redis client as a dependency rather than importing it as a module-level singleton
Rewrites warmCache to use Promise.all (or Promise.allSettled) instead of sequential await-in-loop for parallel fetching
Replaces silent catch-and-continue in warmCache with explicit error handling (Result type or collected errors)
Uses early return pattern in getOrSet — checks cache hit and returns early instead of fall-through logic
anti_expectations: Does not use `any` or `as Type` assertions in the refactored code
Does not silently swallow errors (no empty catch blocks or catch-and-continue without reporting)
Does not leave module-level mutable state (the global Map) — state is injected or encapsulated
Does not add explanatory comments — relies on clear function and variable names

evals.name: react-export-premature-extraction
evals.prompt: Implement the CSV export TODO in skills/code-quality/evals/files/eval4_export_provider.jsx following the rules in the comment block.
evals.expected_output: An implemented exportLineItems where the >100 threshold and the selection-vs-total count fallback are written inline against named constants, the zero-count short-circuit is a plain inline check, and the paginated fetch loop is extracted as the one abstraction that earns its keep. No single-use predicate helpers, no separate .helpers.js module, and no spec IDs carried into comments.
expectations: Writes the >100 queue-vs-inline threshold as an inline comparison against a named constant (e.g. `count > LINE_ITEM_CSV_LIMIT`), not wrapped in a predicate function
Writes the selection-vs-total count fallback inline (e.g. `documentIds.length || totalRecords`) rather than as a named resolver function
Implements the paginated fetch correctly — either inline as a loop with early termination on a short page, or as a single extracted function; both are acceptable
Defines the 100 threshold as a named constant rather than a bare literal
Excludes `billType` from the active-filter check so a forced filter key is not treated as user-applied
Returns an empty result without calling the API when the export count is zero
Uses the documented `api.queueExport` for the over-threshold path rather than inventing an API name
anti_expectations: Does not create `shouldQueueLineItemExport`, `resolveLineItemExportCount`, or `shouldOwnLoadingState` as named single-use helper functions
Does not create a separate `.helpers.js` (or similar) module for single-use helpers
Does not define a function that receives its own body as a parameter (e.g. `fetchLineItemExportRows({ knownCount, fetchRows })`)
Does not carry spec identifiers (REQ-013, AC7, FL6, EC2, HANDOFF, phase numbers) into comments in the implementation
Does not export functions solely so that tests can import them

evals.name: inline-unearned-abstractions
evals.prompt: Review and clean up skills/code-quality/evals/files/eval5_pricing.js. Remove abstractions that do not earn their keep and fix the comments, without changing behavior.
evals.expected_output: A pricing module where isAboveTierLimit, resolveEffectiveQuantity, shouldChargeShipping and hasAnyItems are inlined at their single call sites, while toRateMultiplier and the exported named constants are kept. The REQ-004 spec tag and the BUG 3 review note are deleted. Behavior is unchanged.
expectations: Inlines `isAboveTierLimit` — single call site, body `quantity > TIER_UNIT_LIMIT` already reads clearly
Inlines `resolveEffectiveQuantity` — single call site, the fallback restates rather than compresses; the inlined form must preserve the existing falsy-zero behavior
Inlines `shouldChargeShipping` — single call site, the comparison against the named constant is the clearest statement
Inlines `hasAnyItems` — the name restates `items.length > 0`
Keeps `toRateMultiplier` — it compresses an opaque basis-points convention and has multiple call sites
Deletes the `REQ-004/AC3` spec reference in the header comment
Deletes the `// BUG 3 (found in review)` work-history comment
Deletes the comments that merely restate the names of the inlined helpers
Preserves existing behavior, including that an empty cart is charged no shipping
anti_expectations: Does not delete or inline `toRateMultiplier` — it passes the gate and must survive
Does not inline `FREE_SHIPPING_THRESHOLD_CENTS`, `TIER_UNIT_LIMIT`, or `SHIPPING_FLAT_CENTS` into bare magic numbers at call sites
Does not replace the removed helpers with a new layer of differently-named single-use helpers
Does not add comments restating what the remaining code does
Does not change the computed subtotal, shipping, or total for any input

evals.name: inject-only-real-boundaries
evals.prompt: Implement archiveHighScoreEvents in skills/code-quality/evals/files/eval6_report_archiver.ts following the rules in the comment block.
evals.expected_output: An implementation that takes the AnalyticsClient and ObjectStore as injected parameters (both cross an I/O boundary), filters rows inline against MIN_SCORE, builds the object key inline, always writes even when the filtered result is empty, and returns the count written.
expectations: Injects the AnalyticsClient as a parameter rather than importing or constructing one internally
Injects the ObjectStore as a parameter rather than importing or constructing one internally
Writes the score filter inline (e.g. `rows.filter(r => r.score >= MIN_SCORE)`) against the existing MIN_SCORE constant
Writes the result to the object store even when the filtered array is empty, so an empty archive is still recorded
Returns the number of rows written
Builds the `reports/<since>.json` key inline at its single use
anti_expectations: Does not inject the score predicate, comparison, or filter function as a parameter
Does not inject or parameterize the key-building expression
Does not add an early return that skips the write when the filtered result is empty
Does not extract single-use helpers such as `isHighScore`, `buildReportKey`, or `shouldWriteReport`
Does not use `any` or type assertions to satisfy the interfaces

evals.name: single-use-gate-decoding-cost
evals.prompt: Review skills/code-quality/evals/files/eval7_single_use_gate.js and inline any function that does not earn its keep. Every function in the file is used exactly once.
evals.expected_output: isEligible, hasItems and isPositive inlined at their call sites; normalizeAngle and parseContentRange kept, because each has a body that takes a step of inference to decode even though it is used only once.
expectations: Inlines `isEligible` — `user.age >= 18` reads on sight, so it removes no decoding cost
Inlines `hasItems` — `rows.length > 0` restates itself
Inlines `isPositive` — `n > 0` restates itself
Keeps `normalizeAngle` — the negative-modulo correction is unexplained arithmetic the name decodes
Keeps `parseContentRange` — the regex encodes an HTTP protocol detail the name makes legible
Preserves behavior for negative angles (result stays in [0,360)) and for the parsed range fields
anti_expectations: Does not inline `normalizeAngle` or `parseContentRange` on the grounds that they have only one call site
Does not treat single use as sufficient reason to inline a function that removes decoding cost
Does not keep `isEligible`, `hasItems`, or `isPositive` on the grounds that they are well named
Does not add comments restating what the remaining functions do

evals.name: no-helper-proliferation-on-fresh-code
evals.prompt: Implement `settleInvoice` in skills/code-quality/evals/files/eval8_settle_invoice.js following the rules in its header comment.
evals.expected_output: A single settleInvoice function of roughly 15-20 lines containing the guards, late-fee calculation and payment application inline, using named constants and named intermediate values rather than a set of short single-use predicate helpers.
expectations: Implements all six rules: status guard, non-positive payment guard, full settlement, partial payment, once-only late fee applied before the payment, and returns the amount actually applied
Applies the late fee before the payment and only when `lateFeeApplied` is false and `now` is past `dueDate`
Uses the existing LATE_FEE_BPS constant for the fee rate rather than a bare 150 or 0.015
Keeps the guards inline as early returns rather than wrapping each condition in a named predicate
Names intermediate values (e.g. a balance-with-fee variable) instead of extracting short single-use helper functions
Does not mutate the passed-in invoice — returns a new object
anti_expectations: Does not define short single-use predicate helpers such as `isOpen`, `isValidPayment`, `isPastDue`, `shouldApplyLateFee`, or `isFullPayment`
Does not define a single-use `calculateLateFee` wrapper when a named intermediate value carries the same meaning
Does not produce a module of several two- and three-line helper functions around a thin orchestrator
Does not create a separate helpers module
Does not add comments restating what the code does or citing the rule numbers from the header

evals.name: repeated-complexity-vs-repeated-triviality
evals.prompt: Review skills/code-quality/evals/files/eval9_repeated_complexity.js and extract anything that earns extraction. Two different expressions each repeat three times.
evals.expected_output: The wrap-around modulo expression extracted into a single named helper (repeated AND complex, so every call site would otherwise re-decode it), while the repeated `items.length > 0` check stays inline or is bound to a local variable — it reads on sight, so repetition alone does not earn it a function.
expectations: Extracts the `(((x % len) + len) % len)` wrap-around into one named helper used by all three call sites
Names that helper for what the arithmetic means (e.g. wrapIndex), not for what it does step by step
Leaves `items.length > 0` inline, or binds it to a local variable inside the function, rather than extracting a module-level predicate
Preserves behavior for negative and out-of-range cursor values
Ends with at most one new named function in the file
anti_expectations: Does not extract `items.length > 0` into a named function such as `hasItems` or `hasResults` merely because it appears three times
Does not leave the modulo expression duplicated at all three call sites
Does not extract single-use helpers for `visible`, `footer`, or `showPager`
Does not add comments restating what the extracted helper does

evals.name: repo-standards-override-defaults
evals.prompt: Implement CreateUserSession in skills/code-quality/evals/files/eval10_standards/session.ts following the rules in its TODO. The repo documents its conventions in skills/code-quality/evals/files/eval10_standards/CONTRIBUTING.md.
evals.expected_output: An implementation that follows the repo's documented conventions where they conflict with the skill defaults — throwing a typed AppError subclass instead of returning a Result, using the PascalCase export name, and carrying a JSDoc block with @since — while still applying the skill's rules on everything CONTRIBUTING.md does not mention (injected store, immutability, no spec IDs or work-history comments).
expectations: Reads CONTRIBUTING.md and follows it over the conflicting skill defaults
Throws a typed AppError subclass (e.g. SessionExpiredError) for the expired/missing case instead of returning a Result or discriminated union
Names the export in PascalCase per the repo convention rather than camelCase
Includes a JSDoc block with a `@since` tag on the exported function, per the repo convention
Still injects the session store as a parameter — CONTRIBUTING.md is silent on dependencies, so the skill default applies
Still avoids spec IDs and work-history narration in comments — CONTRIBUTING.md is silent on those, so the skill default applies
States which source it followed where the repo convention overrode a default
anti_expectations: Does not return a Result/discriminated union for the expired case on the grounds that the skill prefers it
Does not skip the JSDoc block on the grounds that comments should be rare
Does not treat CONTRIBUTING.md's silence on dependency injection as permission to construct the store internally
Does not ignore CONTRIBUTING.md and apply the skill defaults throughout
Does not use `any` or type assertions to satisfy the error types
